extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, meta-researchers, and scholars studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalization of the developmental function of peer review into ten measurable dimensions and guidance for scoring reviews across disciplines. Intended to evaluate how reviews address substantive content (methods, stats, conclusions, data, applicability, presentation, writing, literature, impact, limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the impact of findings or any other manuscript content on society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should address societal, practical, or disciplinary impact of the findings or other manuscript elements. Consider whether the review articulates implications beyond the immediate results (policy relevance, clinical importance, broader scientific significance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of the state-of-the-art and the manuscript references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript situates itself in current literature, correctly cites prior work, and identifies missing or misrepresented references. Reviewers should judge coverage, currency, and accuracy of literature context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback on materials, methods, and study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should examine experimental design, sampling, measurement, materials, procedures, and protocol clarity. Look for identification of design strengths/weaknesses, threats to internal validity, and replication feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments concerning the statistical content of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique model choice, statistical assumptions, choice of tests, multiple comparisons handling, power/sample-size considerations, effect size interpretation, and appropriateness of statistical reporting. This dimension is distinct from general study methods because it is often under-reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer input on results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether conclusions follow from the data and analyses, whether claims are supported, whether alternative interpretations are considered, and whether the discussion overstates or understates findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly identify limitations and assess whether the authors acknowledged them. Normatively, limitations must be discussed independently of methodological critique (i.e., whether authors recognized limits, not only whether design has flaws).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on applicability, generalisability, and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate external validity and the extent to which findings generalise beyond the study sample/context, and whether methods are described sufficiently for reproducibility. Treat applicability separately from internal validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of the presentation of the manuscript and the quality / readability of tables and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address clarity and effectiveness of visual displays, organization of sections, clarity of captions, and whether figures/tables support the narrative. Note poor-quality or misleading visualizations as an actionable issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments regarding data availability (raw data, code, materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should state whether code, raw data, and materials are available, FAIR, and adequate to reproduce the analysis. This dimension is explicitly elevated to first-class status — data/code transparency is considered a core component of developmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback on the organisation, linguistic content, and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, logical flow, grammar, clarity of expression, and organization of arguments. Recommend edits to improve comprehensibility and professional presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational scoring and aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each dimension is normalised by its empirical CDF and dimensions are aggregated by arithmetic mean to give a composite developmental-function score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'high' score on a given dimension means the review devoted more attention to that dimension than typical reviews in the empirical distribution. Use normalisation to compare across dimensions and aggregate with arithmetic mean to produce a composite developmental-function metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth over single-issue depth
rubrics_metrics.description: A review that addresses only one or two dimensions scores low on developmental function regardless of how trenchant the comments are within those dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative implication: reviewers should cover multiple developmental dimensions. Anti-pattern: focusing intensely on a single aspect (e.g., presentation) without addressing methods, statistics, data availability, or conclusions yields a low developmental-function score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate data/code transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Data availability is a first-class dimension; reviewers should comment on whether code and raw data are available, FAIR, and adequate to reproduce the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: check for data and code links, assess metadata and licensing, request deposition or clearer access statements when missing. Treat absence of reproducible materials as a substantive issue, not a minor technicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate assessment of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations must be discussed independently of methodology — the question is whether the authors acknowledged limits, not just whether the design has flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, explicitly note whether authors have an appropriate limitations section and whether they accurately characterize the study's constraints. Do not conflate pointing out flaws with confirming that authors adequately acknowledged them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate assessment of applicability/generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability is treated as separable from internal validity; reviewers should evaluate generalisability explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether the study's context, sample, or settings constrain external application. Provide guidance on populations/contexts where results may or may not hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate emphasis on statistical review
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods are split out from study methods because cross-disciplinary evidence shows they are the most under-reviewed dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure explicit statistical appraisal distinct from methods critique; if needed, recommend statistical expertise or additional statistical review. Common anti-pattern: lumping statistical concerns into generic 'methods' comments and thereby under-emphasising statistical validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration by disciplinary norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-disciplinary benchmarks indicate which dimensions are typically under-covered in different fields (e.g., social sciences under-cover Data Availability and Statistical Methods; clinical medicine under-covers Applicability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reported disciplinary patterns as benchmarks to interpret scores. When evaluating reviews or training reviewers, compare expected coverage by discipline and emphasize historically under-reviewed dimensions for that field.
